claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning interatomic potential with on-the-fly validation can accurately reproduce solid and liquid free-energy landscapes near fusion.
The proposed workflow can retain the vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration entropy contributions relevant to fusion.
Fe–Ni is a well-characterized binary metallic benchmark system for this application.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a multicomponent high-entropy alloy suitable for extending the workflow.
The proposed potential will be trained on sparse ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots.
Periodic recalibration will identify and incorporate configurations exhibiting significant electron–vibration and anharmonic effects.
Testing will cover both solid and liquid phases within approximately 10–20% above or below the measured melting point.
The workflow will begin with binary systems and then be extended to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Accurate reconstruction of the potential-energy surface by the ML potential will enable reconstruction of phase free-energy differences.
Continuous validation enables the ML potential to capture vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
Active learning reduces computational expense by replacing extended ab initio molecular dynamics with targeted ab initio snapshots.
Periodic validation systematically incorporates rare configurations that strongly influence electron–vibration coupling and anharmonicity.
Systematic incorporation of rare configurations will maintain high fidelity in calculated free energies.
The proposed workflow will be at least ten times faster than full ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed workflow will be approximately two to three times faster than TOR-TILD.
The proposed workflow will estimate free energies within 5–10% of explicit evaluations.
Full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD calculations on Fe–Ni can serve as benchmark controls.
Deviations greater than 10% in phase free-energy differences or derived thermodynamic observables relative to explicit benchmarks will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary field says the method is already validated within the fusion-temperature window, whereas the falsification design presents that validation as a future experiment.
